nodes.notes: 1) Classification: elementwise+reduction fusion (RMSNorm reduction over D=4096 + elementwise multiply with weight + RoPE rotation over head_dim pairs). Output (B,S,D) fp16. 2) Math: per (b,s) row, var=mean(x^2), inv=rsqrt(var+eps); n_i=x_i*inv*w_i (fp16). Then for each head h, pairs (i,i+half) with half=64: y[..,i]=n_i*cos[s,i]-n_{i+half}*sin[s,i]; y[..,i+half]=n_i*sin[s,i]+n_{i+half}*cos[s,i]. cos/sin shared across heads. 3) Layout: x contiguous (B,S,D); per row of D=4096 contains 32 heads of 128. RoPE cos/sin (S,64) fp32 broadcast. weight (D,) fp16. 4) Regimes: small-batch latency-bound; this case B*S=16384 rows, D=4096 -> 16384 blocks, plenty of parallelism, BW-bound. 5) Knobs: one program per (b,s) row, BLOCK_D covers full 4096 in one pass; load x row once, compute sum-of-squares in fp32, then second pass to write normed*rope. Alternatively single-pass keep x in regs. Cast cos/sin to fp16 once or on the fly. 6) Skeleton: pid=row_id; offs=arange(D); x=load; xf=x.to(fp32); ss=sum(xf*xf); inv=rsqrt(ss/D+eps); n=(xf*inv)*w; reshape implicit: split D into (32 heads,128); for each pair index i in [0,half), load cos[s,i], sin[s,i]; compute. Use index tricks: half-mask. 7) Families: (a) Single-kernel full fusion 1 row/program (TOP - working set ~8KB fits in regs); (b) Two-pass kernel (rmsnorm then rope) - extra global RT, worse; (c) Tile over D with shared-mem reduction - unnecessary since row fits.

action.description: Single Triton kernel: one program per (B*S) row. Load the full D=4096 fp16 row into registers, compute sum-of-squares in fp32, rsqrt, multiply by weight, then apply RoPE by loading cos/sin (head_dim/2=64) once and broadcasting across 32 heads. Write output. BLOCK_D=4096 or split into 2 chunks if needed. Use num_warps=8 and num_stages=1-2.
action.rationale: Eliminates intermediate global tensors and matches BW roofline. Single pass over x.

kernel_summary: Fused RMSNorm + rotate_half RoPE on fp16 (B=8,S=2048,D=4096,heads=32,head_dim=128). Per (b,s) row: reduce sum(x^2) over D (fp32 accum), scale by rsqrt and weight, then for each of 32 heads apply 2D rotation between halves using shared cos/sin tables of size (S,64). Memory-bound: ~256MB DRAM traffic, BW roofline ~0.29ms on 896GB/s. Key constraints: row size 8KB fp16 fits in registers/shared per block; cos/sin (fp32) tables need cast-to-fp16 or fp32 multiply with fp16; output dtype fp16. Goal: single fused Triton kernel, one program per row, to beat torch.compile by avoiding intermediate (B,S,D) tensors and minimizing global round-trips.
open_questions: Does keeping a full D=4096 fp32 row in registers cause spills with 8 warps, or should we keep x in fp16 and convert lanes on the fly?
Should cos/sin be precomputed/cast to fp16 (saving BW + register) given the multiply happens after fp16 cast of normed values?
Best BLOCK_D / num_warps combo on Blackwell sm_100: BLOCK_D=4096 num_warps=8 vs BLOCK_D=2048 num_warps=4?
Is L2 sufficient to cache x rows for a two-pass design (8KB/row * concurrent rows) avoiding doubled DRAM traffic?
How to index the RoPE pair (i, i+half) within a single BLOCK_D load — using mask/where on offs, or splitting loads into two halves of size 2048?
Does the eps placement (inside rsqrt) and fp32 accumulation order match HF/PyTorch closely enough for atol≈1e-3 fp16 tolerance?
Will the kernel autotune over num_warps={4,8} and num_stages provide consistent wins, or fixed config sufficient?
Are there gains from precomputing cos/sin as a fused (S,head_dim) fp16 tensor to allow a single contiguous load per head instead of two half-loads?
